thread.title: Tech stocks will be hurt less by the end of central-bank stimulus programs

author: morningstar.com
title: Tech stocks will be hurt less by the end of central-bank stimulus programs
text:
By Thomas H. Kee Jr.
Buybacks could still buoy their shares
The fourth quarter is soon upon us, and major changes are happening with the Federal Reserve and European Central Bank as the calendar turns.
Still, technology investors have the wind at their back.
As the third quarter ends and the fourth quarter begins, the Fed and the ECB will reduce their asset-repurchase programs, removing an additional $65 billion a month in global liquidity. But that doesn't paint the entire picture.
A year ago, the global-liquidity injections by those central banks totaled $60 billion a month. Now with the $65 billion reduction slated for the fourth quarter, the net drain on liquidity by those central banks is $135 billion a month. That's a $195 billion drop in global liquidity.
That shift has already hurt the bond market, but it can hurt other assets too.
Fortunately, for technology companies especially, the liquidity that has been focused on those companies remains ample. The share-repurchase programs by Apple (AAPL), Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOGL) and Cisco Systems (CSCO), just to name a few, are still flowing like a river.
The interest that investors have in large-cap technology stocks, when coupled with those additional share-repurchase programs, could give them a bid that the other markets do not have.
A concern is that investors like to buy the tech sector using an ETF, such as the Invesco QQQ Trust Series I (QQQ) or the ProShares Ultra QQQ (QLD), but not every company in those ETFs is engaged in aggressive share-repurchase programs. Some of those technology stocks are likely to benefit from what's happening to others as a result, so beware of excessive valuations in the tech space once the share-repurchase programs revert to normal.
Thomas H. Kee Jr. is a former Morgan Stanley broker and founder of Stock Traders Daily (http://www.stocktradersdaily.com/).
-Thomas H. Kee Jr.;
